newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU continues probe into Thomson recapitalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU continues probe into Thomson recapitalisation.

text.p: The European Commission will continue its investigation into the proposed recapitalisation of Thomson SA, despite the suspension of the privatisation of the electronics and defence giant, a Commission source said on Wednesday.
But it was unlikely to give its verdict on December 18, as originally expected, the source told reporters.
"The Commission must assess the aid aspect. That is separate from the sale," the source said.
EU competition officials met French Treasury officials and Thomson representatives to discuss the issue on Monday.
The French government had agreed at the meeting to provide written commitments and assurances regarding the injection of 10.8 billion francs into Thomson, the source said.

"The major part" of the money was intended for Thomson Multimedia which was set to be sold to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea before the operation was cancelled by a French privatisation commission.

The source hinted that as the case stood on Monday, the EU would probably have taken a favourable approach to the capital injection, which amounts to state aid, if the French government provided necessary commitments.
The source declined to give details on the guarantees sought from the French government.

The Commission usually insists that a company getting aid goes through a restructuring exercise that ensures its future viability. It also normally insists that in return for the state money the company's market share be frozen while it is being restructured.

The cancellation of the sale would almost certainly involve new talks betwen the Commission and the French authorities. The source said, referring to a report in the French satyrical weekly Le Canard Enchaine that Daewoo had agreed to share the restructuring burden up to seven billion francs.
